approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a bounded population of molecules scored in the current task. It favors high score quantiles when choosing the first parent and a distinct crossover partner, generates fresh graphs through crossover and ordinary atom/bond edits, and admits stable canonical identities. A Gaussian-process predictor trained on the complete accepted-score archive uses count fingerprints and correlated posterior samples to select the next evaluation batch from a larger fresh pool. Each accepted offspring immediately enters score/serial-ordered survivor competition and can breed at the next suggestion; all accepted labels also enter the next fit, including records that do not survive. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled.
approach.novelty: This ablation removes just the newest accepted cohort's immediate breeding opportunity. First-parent and partner selection use the ordinary bounded population as it stood before the most recent nonempty accepted feedback cohort, while current survival and full predictor learning still update immediately. The next real nonempty cohort releases the preceding cohort to this breeding snapshot if it survived ordinary retention. Earlier siblings froze breeders to the initial molecules, changed survivor capacity or recency, or changed source probabilities and draw scheduling. None isolated this single-cohort consumer delay. The test asks whether prompt recursive use adds value beyond later recursive use.

observed_bottleneck: The unresolved Parent boundary is immediate reuse of newly accepted offspring: it makes the very newest accepted population available before another real feedback cohort arrives, and the value of that first opportunity has not been isolated. Actual Parent summary.json and run.log files for all supplied Search seeds are present and successful: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. A read-only reconstruction of all fifteen published Parent optimizer logs verifies 110295 parent draws, including 105073 from generated accepted offspring. Of these, 31115 use the newest accepted cohort immediately (21452 first and 9663 partner draws), from 2321 distinct newest records; 2450 distinct newest records have positive immediate support, and 1923 accepted products have a newest-cohort generating source. Newest positive support and a different passive one-cohort-delay law occur in 419 of 420 post-initial suggestion states. These are actual timing opportunities and passive same-history laws, not an evaluated delayed Child. The Parent has 4350 accepted offspring, 629 best-parent beats and 258 sequential incumbent advances with total measured increment 5.807663080367226. Static-initial breeding n-4d4b5eafa8b3 lost 0.260205546950089 and every endpoint while retaining full learning; it supports recursive access overall but cannot identify zero-delay necessity. Capacity removal n-1fdd6af786dc lost 0.023494864529627013 despite more parent wins. Nonincumbent-first removal n-9da98b015a09 lost 0.05581647713547766 despite more, smaller incumbent advances; partner-exclusion removal n-60350f969287 lost 0.03199243583539332 despite productive self offspring. Thus the immediate edge is materially exposed, but source quality, event counts, survival, support and later use must be measured separately from absolute endpoints.
hypothesis: Remove only immediate access of the newest nonempty accepted observe cohort to both breeding-parent consumers by using the original bounded greedy population from immediately before that cohort; release a cohort after the next real nonempty accepted cohort, while ordinary current survival and full accepted-archive GP learning remain immediate.

finding_summary.headline: One-cohort breeding delay preserves recursion but lowers mean final Top-1 by 0.052370.
finding_summary.insights:
Prompt reuse contributes beyond simply allowing accepted offspring to breed eventually, under this fixed optimizer, feedback cadence and evaluation budget. Full learning from new scores remained immediate, so withholding those labels from the predictor does not explain this contrast. The previous static-initial experiment established the value of recursive access overall; this result adds a narrower timing answer while preserving that earlier finding.

More local parent wins are compatible with worse search when breeding sources themselves have lower scores. Similar numbers of distinct reused offspring also conceal shallower scored ancestry: maximum depth fell from 23 to 14. These observations narrow the explanations, but do not establish that ancestry depth, source quality or molecular age caused the endpoint loss. Support, ranks, sampling probabilities, random consumption and subsequent adaptive histories all changed together.

The molecular assessment found rich ring systems, useful amine and carbonyl arrangements, and seed-dependent scaffold families in both runs, alongside recurring reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry. Chemically mixed alternatives and task-specific improvements remain visible. The timing contrast identifies no chemical mediator or general shortage of rings or functional groups. Whole-foundation value, interaction with the separate learner control, and reliability beyond these three matched seeds remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The delay operated in all fifteen task/seed runs. None of 110,134 parent draws used the newest accepted cohort, although 2,522 newly accepted molecules had positive support under the immediate current-population law. Later recursion remained active: 2,409 accepted offspring eventually bred, producing 4,031 accepted products with generated parents. All 435 full-archive predictor fits and all 435 fresh pools completed. Maturity did not guarantee use: 841 retained offspring never received positive support and another 56 supported offspring were never drawn. The final 150 offspring lacked a future maturation event; the preceding 150 matured only at terminal feedback and had no subsequent breeding opportunity.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.543300, a paired change of -0.052370 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.115073, -0.011259 and -0.030776. Ten task/seed endpoints declined and five improved: the exceptions were two zaleplon runs, two median-similarity runs and one decoration-hopping run. Docking and sitagliptin declined in every seed. Seed macro population SD decreased slightly, from 0.026593 to 0.024744.

Strict offspring-versus-best-parent wins increased from 629 to 877, but mean absolute offspring scores fell from 0.385256 to 0.321667 and mean best-generating-parent scores fell from 0.470456 to 0.384678. Incumbent advances fell from 258 to 219, with total increment magnitude decreasing from 5.807663 to 5.022119 across the fifteen searches.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles and aryl amines vary by seed, with reactive heteroatom halides, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment of n-4a649366619a reads every row in the 15 supplied Child trajectories and the 15 published search trajectories of code Parent n-62daf219c70a. Each task has 900 Child observations across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, including 870 optimizer observations. No requested trajectory path is missing, no task is omitted, and context.comparison separately confirms child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with the same three matched seeds and no profile mismatch. The bounded digest pools seeds: its final excerpt is from seed 2, so it is not treated as a representative terminal molecule for every seed. The output is predominantly medium-sized to large, branched, aromatic and heterocyclic; it includes recognizable amides, lactams, esters, phenols, ethers and available aliphatic amines. The digest ring-closure incidences range from 0.9494 to 0.9862 and aromatic-token incidences from 0.9310 to 0.9782; these measure the presence of string features, not aromatic atom fractions or geometric feasibility. Different seeds reach distinct families, while their high-scoring neighborhoods repeatedly modify the same frameworks. This supports moderate structural diversity with local concentration, not global scaffold collapse. Drug-like functional arrangements coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, dense bridges, small unsaturated rings, cyclic cumulenes, very large elaborations and occasional tiny fragments. RDKit perception from the actual trajectories finds no parsing failures among the 4,350 Child optimizer records, but this is only graph validation. It identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,035 of those records, while the digest reports stereocentre-string and charge-string incidences of 0.0 for every task. Neutral notation does not imply absence of protonatable amines. Size, ring counts and motif counts below are deterministic readings of the observed molecules, not new oracle scores or synthesis predictions. Plausibility judgments concern apparent chemical environments; routes, stability, conformations and protonation have not been demonstrated. Full source hashes, per-seed descriptors, exact score values and initial/best/worst/final records are in .slots/round-0025-slot-2/molecular_audit.json, generated by molecular_audit.py using RDKit 2023.09.6. All report cited_smiles are actual Child strings authorized by the immutable request. Parent comparisons use its published trajectories through the supplied evidence index; the indexed Parent molecular report supplies historical gap provenance. These chemical associations do not attribute an effect to the breeder delay, establish activation, identify a chemical mediator, or decide contribution.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer records have a median of 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, usually with extensive aromatic character; the digest aromatic-token incidence is 0.9667. The three seed leaders each have 24 heavy atoms but differ substantially. Seed 0, evaluation 262, has a benzene-fused four-member unsaturated ring, a methoxy group and an N-fluorinated amidine linked to fluoropyridine. Seed 1, evaluation 270, is an alkyl/vinyloxy-substituted indole-like aromatic system with an N-Cl bond and a pyridyl ketone. Seed 2, evaluation 179, has a methylthio substituent, an N-methyl-N-phenyl amide and a fused N/O-containing ring system; RDKit perceives a four-member ring containing aromatic-labelled atoms. Thus the output can supply compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements, but even the halogen-free seed-2 leader needs a ring-geometry assessment. Other seed-2 high records contain N-hydroxy amides or ring-bound cumulated double bonds. These are more complex and chemically questionable than a uniform collection of ordinary aryl amides. The Parent also favors compact aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl or imino structures, with N-halogen substitution in its seed leaders.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 376 of 870 Child optimizer records, compared with 445 of 870 Parent records; ordinary carbon-bound halogen substitution is chemically distinct. These frequencies do not establish the effect of removing the bonds.

The seed-2 aromatic-labelled four-member N/O ring and cyclic-cumulene relatives raise geometric and synthetic concerns. N-hydroxy amides and methylthio groups require their own environment-specific assessment and are not automatically equivalent to the more reactive N-halogen examples.
missing_features: Consistently conventional bond environments around the favorable compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are missing from the leading set: the seed-0 and seed-1 leaders use N-halogen bonds, while the halogen-free seed-2 leader has an unusual small aromatic-labelled ring.

Geometrically credible alternatives to the small fused rings and endocyclic cumulated bonds are not established at the same scores. The record does not identify an absent target motif that could be supplied simply by adding another ring or nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl amide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.4175635604843711, 0.4597940970593737 and 0.45766047024715; the paired Parent leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. The direction therefore differs by seed. Seed 1 evaluation 201 retains an alkyl/methoxy/N-chloro aromatic core but lacks the substantial carbonyl-linked aromatic region and scores only 0.00184649918126606; seed 0 evaluation 282 is ethene at 0.0. The visible association favors an organized, moderately sized aromatic plus carbonyl/imino arrangement over fragments or an isolated decorated core. This is not an isolated proof of any one functional-group requirement. Seed 2 evaluation 190 reaches 0.4491253474628456 with a fused N-heterocycle/N-hydroxy aryl amide and no halogen, countering a universal halogen requirement. Its cyclic-cumulene/N-bromo-amide relative at evaluation 253 reaches 0.4514335070299504, so high scores do not exclude difficult chemistry. The seed-2 last proposal at evaluation 300 scores 0.3995736468848427; it is not that seed's best molecule.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled optimizer records have a median of 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, with ring-closure-string incidence 0.9747. The seed-0 leader at evaluation 286 has 29 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings: a nitrogen-rich fused dione joined through an N-N-containing linkage to an aza-aromatic bicyclic region, with methyl, fluoromethyl and carbon-bound chlorine groups. The seed-1 leader at evaluation 296 has 33 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, linked aza-aromatic/carbonyl/ether regions, aryl Br/F, chloromethyl and chloromethyl-ether substituents. Seed 2 instead favors a 37-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring biheteroaryl/anilino system with carbon-bound fluorines and multiple ester groups, including a vinyl ester. These ester-bearing graphs are more conventional locally than the reactive substituents in some other seeds, although their size, flexibility and synthetic route remain concerns. At the extreme, an evaluated proposal has 112 heavy atoms; this is not the size of the leaders. The Parent seed-0 leader has a different compact fused/bridged carbonyl-thione organization, including O-F and a halomethyl ether, while its other seeds retain distinct linked aromatic families.
liabilities: The seed-1 leader contains a chloromethyl ether and other halogenated termini; the seed-0 leader contains an N-N linkage. These deserve local reactivity assessment, without treating ordinary aryl halides or every N-N bond as inherently unmakeable.

Multiple ester groups, broad aromatic surfaces and large outlier elaborations add flexibility or synthetic burden. The seed-2 conventional ester family is a counterexample to universal heteroatom-halide dependence, but no route or stability record is supplied.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of alternative connected heterocyclic arrangements is not demonstrated within each seed: the Child does not recover the Parent seed-0 leading organization at its observed score, while its seed-2 family exceeds the paired Parent. No common absent atom or decoration explains both cases.

Less reactive peripheral alternatives that retain useful aromatic connectivity need chemical feasibility evidence. The tied ester/ether/thiono variants show that peripheral chemical identity can change without an observed score improvement, rather than establishing a specific required substituent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.6297226207556194, 0.617581553779641 and 0.6379551820728291, versus Parent values 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The large seed-0 separation coexists with a seed-2 reversal; it cannot be summarized as one missing ring class. A smaller fused nitrogen-carbonyl fragment in Child seed 0 evaluation 138 scores 0.5183568573060292, and methane at evaluation 278 has the observed 0.5 floor. The higher records preserve combined, connected heteroaromatic regions and substituent context. Seed 2 evaluation 260 and variants at evaluations 277 and 286 all score 0.6379551820728291 despite changing an ester region to an ether or replacing a carbonyl oxygen with sulfur. These exact score ties show limited local discrimination among chemically different peripheral groups; they do not establish equal stability or a need for the less conventional group. Its final proposal scores 0.6284882553704075. The Parent's higher seed-0 arrangement is observed evidence of an alternative organization, not proof that its O-F bond or thione supplies the missing benefit.

per_task.generated_character: The evaluated output is dominated by halogenated aryl groups attached to saturated or partly unsaturated aliphatic nitrogen systems; the median optimizer size is 33 heavy atoms, with three rings and seven rotatable bonds. Seed 0 evaluation 261 is a 32-heavy-atom secondary cyclic amine with a seven-member unsaturated N-ring, an aryl amide, phenol, methoxy and carbon-bound halogens. Seed 1 evaluation 299 is a 31-heavy-atom flexible diaryl chain carrying a primary amine and an N-methyl six-member diazinane-like cyclic aminal, plus phenol and methoxy groups. Seed 2 evaluation 300 has 33 heavy atoms, a related saturated two-nitrogen ring, an amide, an aniline, hydroxymethyl and a chroman-like fused ether ring. The three leaders have two aromatic rings each and recognizable medicinal-chemistry handles, without direct N-halogen or O-halogen bonds. Available aliphatic amines are already abundant: the explicitly defined operational motif occurs in 752 of 870 Child records and all ten highest-score records in each seed. This motif count is not a pKa calculation. The Parent also has aryl/aliphatic-amine leaders, including a flexible tertiary amine and cyclic amine/fused-ring families.
liabilities: Long flexible chains, multiple carbon-bound halogens and cyclic N-C-N aminal environments remain concerns even when no N/O-halogen bond is present. The smaller high-score example retains a potentially reactive alkyl chloride, so compactness alone does not remove local liabilities.

RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 845 of 870 Child optimizer records. Neutral SMILES and absent stereotags leave chemical identity under-specified; they do not imply that the structures are achiral or nonbasic.

Cumulated carbon double-bond centers occur in 41 Child optimizer records, including 37 with the center in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms, but none of the ten highest-score records in each Child seed has one. The pool contains this liability without making it a feature of every leading molecule.
missing_features: Explicit stereochemical identities are missing for the substituted saturated-ring and benzylic arrangements: all seed leaders have unassigned potential tetrahedral centers. The record does not quantify any stereochemical score penalty.

Protonation and local aminal stability are unresolved despite abundant available amines. The missing evidence is a chemically defined, feasible presentation of those centers; recommending the addition of a basic ring nitrogen would misdescribe the existing output.

A transferable exact missing pharmacophore is not identified by the different high-scoring Child and Parent aryl-amine families. Distinct viable arrangements are already visible, and maximal size or aromatic count is not required in this sample.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial large aryl/amide/N-sulfonyl-ring molecule scores 0.01904115112334333. An early N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine derivative in seed 0 evaluation 16 scores 0.00021169315013374197; seed 2 evaluation 26 adds an N-chloro amide and scores 0.00016650955053713697. The Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.8176848497783635, 0.9855368239002947 and 0.9756822893990494, versus Parent values 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. The observed gradient associates higher values with accessible aliphatic amines presented alongside aryl regions, rather than total nitrogen, sulfonyl groups or halogen count. Within the same seed-1 diaryl/diazinane framework, the amino-bearing evaluation 299 scores 0.9855368239002947 while the corresponding alcohol at evaluation 268 scores 0.9738634517805085; the alcohol already scores highly, so the extra primary amine is not a universal requirement. A smaller single-aryl cyclic-amine/chloroalkyl molecule at seed 1 evaluation 261 has 21 heavy atoms and scores 0.9367802047129189. A high recorded value is therefore retained with less aromatic extent and smaller size. These recorded scores do not establish binding, selectivity or the cause of the paired differences.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled optimizer records have a median of 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings. Aromatic surfaces coexist with lactams, dicarbonyl nitrogen rings, alkoxy groups and densely connected saturated centers; halogen-string incidence is only 0.1184. Seed 0 evaluation 279 has 34 heavy atoms and a propyl/ethoxy aza-aromatic region joined into a bridged diaryl dicarbonyl/N-methyl framework, including perceived four- and eight-member rings. Seed 1 evaluation 294 has 33 heavy atoms and an extended fused aromatic nitrogen system with an N-aryl acetyl/ethoxy region and an N-methyl medium-ring lactam. Seed 2 evaluation 272 instead reaches 38 heavy atoms and six rings: an alkylquinoline linked by an ether to a dense nitrogen-rich bridged dicarbonyl system. These are distinct seed families, but high-score neighbors within each family mostly alter short chains, ring segments or local atom identity. The Parent has related quinoline/bridged carbonyl and diaryl-lactam families; its pooled median size is 30 heavy atoms. The functional groups are recognizable, whereas the dense ring junctions and unassigned centers make synthetic accessibility less certain than the graph validity suggests.
liabilities: Dense junctions, small fused rings, medium rings and ring-bound unsaturation create geometric and synthesis questions. More atoms or more ring closures do not certify productive complexity.

Unassigned potential tetrahedral centers occur in 627 of 870 Child records. The absence of cumulated-double-bond strings and the low halogen incidence are real counterexamples to treating those liabilities as universal across the output.
missing_features: Simpler, demonstrably feasible connectivities that preserve the favorable aromatic/nitrogen-carbonyl arrangement are not established at the leading values. Existing local variants show some tolerance, but this does not establish a route or a superior simplified structure.
The bridged and medium-ring molecules lack explicit stereochemical identity and a demonstrated conformational arrangement; aromatic rings and carbonyl acceptors themselves are already present.
Independent feasible alternatives remain limited among high-score neighbors within each seed, although distinct seed families prevent a claim of complete scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.2339854106482522, 0.2243954803839473 and 0.2133714657848147, versus Parent values 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The slightly larger Child families do not have a consistent paired direction. Seed-0 oxygen-containing ring relatives at evaluations 252 and 281 score 0.23236843881072003 and 0.23380677771353114, close to the leading carbon-containing connectivity. The visible reward follows the combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl organization across several local ring variants, not a unique bridge atom. A seed-1 enol/diene side-chain dione lacking the extended aryl arrangement at evaluation 39 scores 0.10284355469137708. Conversely, the oversized repeated aryl/dione structure in seed 0 evaluation 40 scores only 0.11656661085678245, and acetylene at evaluation 245 scores 0.0. Both fragmentation and indiscriminate elaboration can lose the useful organization. The final seed-2 structure scores 0.1890640859763816. The record does not identify an exact missing target motif or show that greater generic ring richness closes the remaining score gap.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer records have a median of 27 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, usually with a compact nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino region. Seed 0 evaluation 272 has 26 heavy atoms: an N-methyl/N-S-substituted fused dione, a phenolic aryl thiol, and an amino-linked fluorocyclobutene. It has no N-F bond, but includes two perceived four-member rings. Seed 1 evaluation 221 has 27 heavy atoms and a fused N-fluorinated dione attached to phenol and a substituted fluorinated five-member imine ring. Seed 2 evaluation 292 has 26 heavy atoms: a fused imino-rich N-heterocycle with N-F, methyl and fluoromethyl groups, attached to a cyclopentadienol carrying a thiono group with an O-F bond. Its leading carbocycle is not a cumulene. However, the full Child sample contains many cyclic cumulenes: the digest cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.1770, corresponding to 154 of 870 records in the audit, versus 45 of 870 Parent records. Compact molecular size therefore coexists with substantial local chemical concerns. The Parent leaders include other fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl structures and, in seed 2, a small cyclic cumulene coupled to a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 378 of 870 Child records and O-halogen bonds in 34; the leading seed-2 thiono O-F and N-F environments are not ordinary carbon-fluorine substitution.

Cumulated carbon double bonds forced into small rings, including the cited four-member example, raise serious geometric concerns. The noncumulated best molecule and the lower prevalence in the Parent prevent conflating this liability with a demonstrated route to higher scores.

Potential stereogenic centers are unspecified, and enolic/imino forms lack chemical-state characterization. Sulfur-containing termini and densely substituted small rings also leave stability and synthesis unresolved.
missing_features: Consistently conventional alternatives preserving the favorable compact polar/fluorinated arrangement are missing from the leading set: separate leaders avoid N-F or cyclic cumulenes, yet still carry other unusual bonds or small-ring connectivities.
Geometric, stereochemical and tautomeric identity of the small unsaturated rings and imino/enolic systems is unresolved. More fluorine or more nitrogen is not an identified missing capability.
The alternative higher-scoring Parent frameworks are not matched chemical controls for the Child; the record does not show which absent substituent or topology would restore their values.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The common initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child seed-0/1/2 leaders score 0.4527359975242378, 0.46072565546609645 and 0.5651057040234259, versus Parent values 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. Within the leading seed-2 imino/thiono framework, changing the methyl substituent at evaluation 271 to fluoromethyl at evaluation 292 raises the recorded value from 0.5440573715317063 to 0.5651057040234259. This is a scaffold-conditioned local substitution observation, not a universal rule to add fluorine. Isolated F at seed 1 evaluation 223 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, and a bulky polyacetal/aryl/dione combination at seed 0 evaluation 39 scores 1.7221553243013507e-29. Compact combined polar and fluorinated organization is favored over isolated fluorine or unconstrained size growth. Seed 0 evaluation 298 scores 0.4341233989477964 while containing a cumulated segment in a four-member ring; seed 2 evaluation 241 has a small cyclic cumulene at 0.3089131810348397. These concerns occur in scored output, but the seed-2 best is noncumulated and the seed-0 best lacks N-F. The last seed-2 complex proposal scores 0.18648889469635047; its late ethane proposal at evaluation 295 scores 8.767937379921204e-21. High recorded reward does not consistently enforce credible chemistry, and no exact missing target pharmacophore follows from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The indexed n-62daf219c70a molecular report attributes this gap to n-c55c3d520a2c and its repeated Search evidence. It is re-observed here in n-4a649366619a relative to n-62daf219c70a under the frozen Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch size 10 and 300 observations per objective. The 4,350 Child optimizer records include 813 with direct N-halogen bonds and 77 with direct O-halogen bonds; these counts overlap and are not a count of distinct affected records. Leaders also include a chloromethyl ether and N-S functionality. Counterexamples are substantial: aryl/aliphatic-amine leaders and the ester-rich linked aromatic family have ordinary carbon-bound halogens without N/O-halogen bonds, and a halogen-free aromatic amide scores highly within its own history. The deficiency concerns local environments, not a general inability to form useful amines, heterocycles or carbon-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining useful aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic graph transformations could distinguish bond environments and offer chemically plausible alternatives while preserving favorable relationships learned from local feedback. The record motivates testing that capability; it does not show that blanket halogen removal or a fixed reactivity filter improves scores. The inherited gap keeps its original source and frozen observation conditions, and this assessment attributes it to no individual component or timing change.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is carried from n-c55c3d520a2c through the indexed n-62daf219c70a report and re-observed in n-4a649366619a on the same frozen three Search Seeds at 300 observations per objective. The Child emits a high-score four-member N/O ring represented with aromatic atoms, dense bridged dicarbonyl systems, and cyclic cumulenes including a four-member-ring example. All 4,350 evaluated Child optimizer graphs parse in RDKit, showing that parsing does not resolve these questions. Ordinary saturated-ring amines and noncumulated high-score alternatives are also present; this is not a universal defect of ring formation or a requirement for exotic unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently separate a valid ring graph from a geometrically credible pattern of fusion, bridging and unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring edits could account for ring size, feasible bond geometry and bridge connectivity while proposing alternative frameworks that preserve learned functional arrangements. Lowercase aromatic notation, ring counts and successful valence checks cannot substitute for this information. The evidence supports assessing local geometry, not banning all small rings or bridges, and establishes no score benefit or component-specific cause.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The indexed Parent report records the same gap for n-c55c3d520a2c and n-62daf219c70a. In n-4a649366619a under the frozen three-seed Search panel, every digest stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, while RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centers in 2,035 of 4,350 optimizer records. Examples include aryl-substituted cyclic amines, fluorinated unsaturated rings and bridged carbonyl systems. Other leading aromatic molecules are achiral under this perception, so not every record requires a stereotag. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but available amine motifs are plainly present.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity when graph edits create potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation and transformations could preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity where applicable, distinguishing stable centers from achiral or configurationally unstable environments. Protonation and tautomerism need separate treatment. These observations identify incomplete chemical specification; they do not demonstrate a stereochemical score penalty, justify an objective-specific state rule, or attribute the omission to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap is inherited from the n-c55c3d520a2c observations recorded in the n-62daf219c70a molecular report and recurs in n-4a649366619a at the frozen Search budget and batch size. The Child evaluates 87 structures with at most three heavy atoms, including late low-score hydrocarbon or halogen fragments, alongside very large repeated or appended ring systems whose observed scores can be low. Higher values generally preserve organized combinations of aromatic, carbonyl and available amine regions. A 21-heavy-atom single-aryl cyclic amine still has a high recorded score in its own history, providing a counterexample to the idea that useful molecules must always be larger or more polyaromatic.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback could guide edits that preserve useful chemical context while simplifying or replacing dispensable regions. The missing consistency does not justify a fixed minimum size, automatic growth preference, or removal of every fragment proposal. The evidence describes evaluated outcomes only and does not attribute them to a component or establish that restricting these moves would improve the final result.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-62daf219c70a report traces this conditional coverage gap to n-c55c3d520a2c. The current n-4a649366619a Search panel again shows repeated peripheral substitutions and local ring-segment changes around each seed's favored aromatic amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine or bridged dicarbonyl family. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct families, and some Child families exceed their paired Parent values while others do not. Ring and aromatic-string incidences are high throughout. These facts support local concentration and chemically mixed alternatives, not global collapse or an inability to invent rings; structural resemblance alone does not establish ancestry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently supply independent, plausible scaffold alternatives within each seed's high-score neighborhood.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could propose feasible alternative connectivities that retain relationships supported by its own observations and evaluate whether those alternatives remain useful. Distinct strings do not establish meaningful scaffold coverage, and more diversity alone is not a demonstrated benefit. The original source, frozen Search conditions and seed-dependent counterexamples must remain attached when this gap is transferred; it is not an attribution to breeder timing or any retained component.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
